>_ Episode 9 · Sep 3, 2026 · 1h 33m

Chinese Room | Does AI Understand? Do LLMs?

Play Episode 9 on YouTube
Watch on YouTube SpotifyApple Podcasts

Can a computer truly understand language, or is it merely following rules and manipulating symbols without meaning? In this episode of Philosophy Programs and Prompts, Casey Hart(@OntologyExplained) and Carl Brown(@InternetOfBugs) dive deep into John Searle’s 1980 seminal paper introducing the Chinese Room thought experiment.

They explore the distinction between Strong and Weak AI, break down the critical difference between syntax and semantics, and discuss whether modern Large Language Models (LLMs) are solving the understanding problem or just running a complex version of symbol retrieval. Along the way, they evaluate major objections to Searle—such as the Systems Reply and the Robot Reply—while examining real-world implications regarding AI agency, simulation vs. reality, and culpability.
